title: Support for Singaporeans affected by international conflicts and efforts to maintain social cohesion
asked: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim asked what community support mechanisms exist to help individuals process the impact of international conflicts, and how global conflicts are unpacked domestically to maintain social harmony and cohesion in Singapore.
answered_by: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
response: The Acting Minister said the Government makes information available in a timely manner, including through Statements to the House, and provides space for civil dialogue. Harmony Circles run inter-ethnic and interfaith initiatives such as the October 2024 Peace and Harmony Dialogue on Gaza and a January 2026 youth seminar on extremism. RLAF, set up by MUIS, provides help channels, and a 2024 Harmony-in-Action campaign raised half a million dollars for Gaza. Asatizah provide counselling, and PERGAS's Asatizah Solace Care is a free, safe and confidential service open to all.

key_points.point: The Government makes information available in a timely manner, including through Statements to this House.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: The Government strives to make such information available in a timely manner, including through Statements to this House.

key_points.point: Space is provided for civil dialogue on these issues and for Singaporeans to contribute constructively.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: It is also important to provide space for civil dialogue on these issues and to allow Singaporeans to contribute in constructive ways.

key_points.point: Racial and Religious Harmony Circles organise inter-ethnic and interfaith initiatives to build trust across communities.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: Our Racial and Religious Harmony Circles organise inter-ethnic and interfaith initiatives to build trust across communities

key_points.point: The Peace and Harmony Dialogue in October 2024 discussed the Gaza situation.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: the Peace and Harmony Dialogue in October 2024 that discussed the Gaza situation

key_points.point: A youth seminar in January 2026 sought to empower youths to act against extremism in the digital age.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: a youth seminar in January 2026 that sought to empower youths to act against extremism in the digital age

key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: The Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation (RLAF), established by the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura or MUIS), provides channels for all Singaporeans to help.

key_points.point: In 2024, Harmony Circles organised the Harmony-in-Action fundraising campaign supporting RLAF's Gaza efforts, raising half a million dollars.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: In 2024, our Harmony Circles organised the Harmony-in-Action fundraising campaign supporting RLAF's Gaza efforts, raising half a million dollars.

key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
